{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
file_path = 'data/sales.csv'
data = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Clean `revenue`: remove commas and convert to float
# Ensure all values are strings and handle potential non-numeric values
# Replace any non-numeric revenue values (like '999999.99' that might be hidden)
data['revenue_clean'] = data['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False)

# Convert to float, coercing errors to NaN
data['revenue_float'] = pd.to_numeric(data['revenue_clean'], errors='coerce')

# Check for any invalid entries after conversion
invalid_entries = data[data['revenue_float'].isna()]
print(f'Number of invalid entries after conversion: {len(invalid_entries)}')

# Check for QA orders (revenue = 999999.99)
qa_orders = data[data['revenue'] == '999999.99']
print(f'Number of QA orders (revenue = 999999.99): {len(qa_orders)}')

# Check for refunded orders
refunded_orders = data[data['status'] == 'refunded']
print(f'Number of refunded orders: {len(refunded_orders)}')

# Check if any revenue is still non-numeric
non_numeric_after_clean = data['revenue_clean'].str.replace('.', '', regex=False).str.isnumeric() | (data['revenue_clean'] == '0')
print(f'Number of entries that are numeric after cleaning: {non_numeric_after_clean.sum()}')

# Display first few cleaned values
print('\nFirst 5 cleaned revenue values:')
data[['revenue', 'revenue_clean', 'revenue_float']].head()"}
